subject.title: Feature: Include trusted sender_name in inbound metadata envelope

question: What sender identity authority should OpenClaw expose as trusted, model-visible inbound metadata for routing and private-message decisions?
rationale: Current code intentionally keeps sender names and per-turn ids out of trusted system metadata, so adding this field changes a security, privacy, and prompt-cache boundary rather than filling a mechanical omission.

options.title: Configured Principal Contract
options.body: Expose a trusted principal only when a stable provider ID matches an operator-configured identity link, while keeping display names in untrusted context.

options.title: Stable Provider ID Contract
options.body: Expose stable channel/provider IDs as trusted metadata and require agents or tools to resolve human-readable labels outside the prompt contract.

options.title: Display Name Contract
options.body: Expose platform-resolved display names directly, accepting a higher privacy and spoofing-review burden for easier agent ergonomics.

recommendation.title: Configured Principal Contract
recommendation.body: Expose a trusted principal only when a stable provider ID matches an operator-configured identity link, while keeping display names in untrusted context.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame places Vincent Koc closest to the trusted inbound metadata and protocol schema lines that would need the final boundary decision.
